correctness.rationale: Follow each of the n initial states. Each a increments modulo n; each effective b encountered at state n−1 also increments the state modulo n. A reset word with A cyclic letters must have pairwise distinct event-count residues B_i mod n, since final state equals i+A+B_i mod n; hence one initial state experiences at least n−1 effective b events. Between successive events it must encounter at least n−1 a letters (the only letter moving it from 0 toward n−1). Thus the specified W occurs as an unavoidable scattered subsequence. Direct image induction shows W reduces Q through S_j={0,…,n−j−1} to {0}; shortest length follows, and no distinct word of equal length can contain W. At one additional symbol every candidate is a single a or b insertion. Endpoint a insertions are good (2), doubled b sites are good (n−1), and in each of n−2 internal a runs all n−3 sites except t=j are good, giving n²−4n+7; n=2 handled separately. The boundary t=j cycle preserves final rank two. Independent separately coded subset-transition DP exhausted both length layers for n=2,…,9; shortest count=1 and excess-one counts all matched formula. An additional product-state BFS search n≤10 found no resetting word avoiding W; this is corroboration not proof for all n.

value.rationale: Černý is a canonical extremal synchronizing automaton, and the result characterizes a necessary pattern shared by ALL reset inputs, not merely one shortest witness. The exact first-excess multiplicity quantifies one-symbol slack and distinguishes redundancy/multiplicity from classical reset threshold. The count is valid for arbitrary n and precisely the natural next-length layer, not an arbitrary finite instance.

final_claim: For the precisely labeled n-state Černý automaton n≥2 with a cyclic increment and b collapsing n−1 to 0, every reset word has W=b(a^(n−1)b)^(n−2) as a scattered subsequence, W alone is the unique shortest reset word of length (n−1)^2, and exactly n²−4n+7 literal reset words occur at one extra symbol.
limitations: No classification for arbitrary automata or greater-than-one excess lengths.
Reversing a and b versus some standard citations is a relabeling and must be normalized when comparing predecessors.
